free_tier.stated: Free plan, quoted: '0.25 vCPU', '256 MB RAM', '1 GB Disk', 'Isolated compute', 'Wakes on the next request', '1 deployment slot per app', 'Custom domains'. The app 'sleeps when idle' and there is 'No card to deploy'. Paid Hobby is 'EUR 3.49 /mo per replica' for 0.5 vCPU, 512 MB RAM and 5 GB disk; a EUR 14.99 credit follows when a payment method is added.

retention.stated: the free app sleeps when idle and wakes on the next request, so a cold start of seconds sits in front of the first request after every idle period.

egress.terms: Bandwidth is unmetered: no egress fees and no per-GB data-transfer meter; a soft fair-use guideline of around 10 TB of outbound per app per month is not a charge
egress.free_allowance: unmetered; soft fair-use guideline of around 10 TB outbound per app per month

record.interface_detail: REST API with an OpenAPI document and X-Api-Key header; the velixir CLI installs as a standalone binary or a.NET global tool; no SSH or SDK documented on the pages read
record.tooling: the velixir CLI (login, deploy, apps, env, db, cache, volume, access-logs) and a REST API with API keys
record.chaining: a free 0.25 vCPU app that serves an API and a cron trigger costs nothing while idle, and the EUR 3.49 Hobby replica is the smallest paid step when a second always-on process is needed.

record.notes: Aggregator claim checked: free-for.dev says 'one app (0.25 vCPU, 256 MB RAM) that sleeps when idle, custom domains with TLS, and no credit card'. The vendor matches, so the gap is zero. Omitted by the aggregator: the 1 GB disk, the one-deployment-slot limit per app, and the EUR 3.49 paid floor. Region is fixed to EU Central by policy, not by a setting the user changes.
